rationale: Adopted exponential backoff with jitter for embeddings API calls to survive rate limiting from the OpenAI provider without failing the write path outright.
Qdrant collection bootstrap is idempotent: ensureCollection checks getCollection before createCollection so repeated CLI invocations never fail on an existing collection.
Dedupe key hashing scheme v1 combines repo, commit, story, entry_type, and source into a single sha256 so near-duplicate writes collapse into one entry.
Config schema validation moved to Zod so memo.config.json fails fast with a readable error instead of an undefined-property crash deep in a command handler.
Search scope defaults to repo but can widen to related repos via --scope related, resolved through the registry of declared relates_to entries in config.
Confidence is inferred from source rather than accepted as a raw flag: agent-authored entries default to high confidence, manual entries to medium, to keep the signal honest.
Duplicate entries offer four resolutions: consolidate, update, replace, or create-new, so a repeated write never silently clobbers an existing decision.
CLI command structure is built on commander, one module per command file registered from a single index entrypoint.
The embeddings adapter wraps the OpenAI text-embedding-3-small model behind a small interface so a future provider swap only touches one adapter file.
Human-readable output uses chalk for color and ora for spinners, scanned into the codebase as an established pattern rather than a one-off choice.
Qdrant operations retry with exponential backoff up to three attempts before surfacing a QDRANT_OPERATION_FAILED error, so transient network blips do not fail a write.
Facet aggregation for memo inspect scrolls the full collection once and tallies orgs, repos, and domains client-side rather than issuing one query per facet.
List filters use exact match on repo, org, tags, and entry_type rather than fuzzy matching, keeping memo list predictable for scripting.
Search filters are built as Qdrant must-clauses so every exact filter narrows the candidate set before semantic scoring ever runs.
Tags and repo/org/domain identifiers are constrained to a kebab-case regex so filenames, filters, and dedupe keys never have to worry about casing drift.
Verbose internal logging is gated behind the MEMO_DEBUG environment variable so normal CLI runs stay quiet by default.
Payload indexes for repo, org, entry_type, source, tags, timestamp_utc, commit, and dedupe_key_sha256 are created once at collection bootstrap to keep exact filters fast.
Entry payloads carry a dedupe_key_version field so a future change to the hashing scheme can migrate old entries without breaking lookups.
The interactive duplicate-resolution prompt only renders on a TTY; JSON and non-interactive callers get a clear VALIDATION_FAILED instead of hanging on stdin.
Deleting by filter first scrolls the matching set to report an accurate deleted count before issuing the batch delete call.
memo tags lists distinct tag values scanned across the collection so agents can discover the existing vocabulary before writing a new entry.
memo read fetches a single entry by id via a bounded scroll with has_id, avoiding a full collection scan for a point lookup.
memo setup init writes memo.config.json with schema_version, repo, org, and domain so later commands can resolve context without repeated flags.
Vector size is fixed at 1536 dimensions to match text-embedding-3-small; changing embedding models later requires a full re-index, documented as a known constraint.
Intent: build a relevance evaluation harness before any ranking change lands, so future ordering work is judged against a recorded baseline instead of intuition.
Outcome: the relevance evaluation harness now seeds a fixture set, runs live queries, and records a baseline top-3 hit rate as the floor for every later Phase 1 story.
The evaluation harness isolates its writes behind MEMO_COLLECTION so seeding fixture data can never land in the production decisions collection.
A standalone bootstrap validation script checks a JSON array of seed entries against a strict Zod schema before any import into the collection.
Husky and lint-staged run ESLint and Prettier on staged files at commit time, scanned in as the existing pre-commit convention for this repository.
ESLint runs typescript-eslint strict-type-checked plus stylistic-type-checked against src/**, favoring caught bugs over convenience escapes.
Invoice generation retries transient vendor timeouts with the same exponential backoff pattern used elsewhere, capped at three attempts before failing the job.
Payment webhooks require a client-supplied idempotency key so a retried webhook delivery never double-charges a customer.
Currency amounts round half-up to the smallest unit at the point of charge, decided after a rounding-drift bug in monthly invoice totals.
Subscription cancellations keep a 3-day grace period before access is revoked, scanned from the support runbook into a durable decision record.
Billing database migrations are structured as sequential numbered files under a migrations directory, applied in order by a single runner.
The billing API gateway applies its own rate limiting per API key, independent of any client-side retry behavior, to protect the payment provider quota.
Outcome: dunning emails now go out on a 1/3/7/14-day cadence after a failed charge, reducing involuntary churn measured over the following quarter.
Sales tax calculation is delegated to a third-party vendor API rather than maintained in-house, given the jurisdictional complexity.
Every billing state change writes an append-only audit log entry, structured with actor, action, and before/after amounts.
Refunds above a threshold require a second approver before the charge reversal is issued, decided after a single-approver refund incident.
Plan-change proration uses a day-based algorithm rather than second-based, trading minor precision for customer-facing simplicity.
Outcome: adding a circuit breaker around the payment provider client cut cascading failures during provider outages to near zero over two incidents.
Invoice PDFs are generated from a single templated renderer so every invoice format change happens in one file instead of per-customer branches.
Billing-service reuses the memo-cli decision store conventions for its own auth token sharing between services, relating this repo back to memo-cli.
